correctness.rationale: The 2026 outer-extremal theorem applies to a norm-attaining nonzero bounded functional on H^(1/2), reducing the problem to a fourth power of an H^2 function. Parseval and the explicit coefficient product produce a three-coordinate quartic whose maximizers are positive interior points. The stationary equations reduce to Q_lambda; Descartes sign variation yields exactly one positive root. An elementary no-boundary-zero homotopy verifies an outer polynomial extremal. Alignment of three nonzero monomial phases establishes equality rigidity. Envelope and uniqueness give strict convexity; the checker reproduces symbolic identities and supplementary numerical comparisons, not a purported exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: The full exact positive supporting family for the first two nontrivial Hardy coefficients is an intrinsic simultaneous-optimization invariant, not a hand-picked slice. Separate known optimal coefficients provide only an unattained crude affine bound, while this result gives the strict support curve, nontrivial quartic root, analytically unique zero-free extremals and full endpoint interpolation. It addresses the natural missing joint question suggested by the established separate coefficient theory.
